title: Buddhism and Jainism: The Shramana Challenge

questions.question: Siddhartha Gautama was born in 563 BCE at:
questions.rationale: The Buddha was born at Lumbini in Nepal, where an Ashokan pillar still marks the spot; his father Suddhodana ruled the Shakya republic from Kapilavastu.

questions.question: The Buddha attained enlightenment under a peepal tree at Uruvela on the river:
questions.rationale: After six years of failed austerity he attained enlightenment at 35 under a peepal tree on the Niranjana — the site of Bodh Gaya. The Rijupalika is the Jain parallel for Mahavira's kaivalya.

questions.question: The Buddha's first sermon, the dharmachakrapravartana, was delivered at:
questions.rationale: The 'turning of the wheel of law' was preached to five disciples at the deer park of Sarnath.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the Four Noble Truths?
options: The soul is permanent and eternal
questions.rationale: The Buddha denied a permanent soul (anatmavada); the truths state suffering, its cause (trishna), its cessation, and the path.

questions.question: The Triratna (three jewels) of Buddhism are:
questions.rationale: Buddha-Dhamma-Sangha is the Buddhist Triratna; right faith-knowledge-conduct is the Jain set, and Vinaya-Sutta-Abhidhamma is the Pali Tipitaka.

questions.question: The Third Buddhist Council, which compiled the Abhidhamma and dispatched missionaries, was held at Pataliputra in 250 BCE under which king?
questions.rationale: Ashoka patronised the Third Council at Pataliputra, presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa; Kanishka later patronised the Fourth at Kashmir.

questions.question: The Bodhisattva ideal and worship of the Buddha's image belong to which branch?
questions.rationale: Mahayana, the 'great vehicle', Sanskrit-using and image-worshipping, developed the Bodhisattva saviour ideal and spread to East Asia.

questions.question: Which vow did Mahavira ADD to the four taught by Parshvanatha?
questions.rationale: Mahavira added brahmacharya (celibacy) to Parshvanatha's four — ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha — completing the five great vows.

questions.question: Anekantavada, the doctrine that truth has many sides, is central to which religion?
questions.rationale: Anekantavada (many-sidedness) and its logical arm syadvada are Jain epistemology, teaching that every statement holds only 'in some respect'.

questions.question: The Jain Agamas were finally written down in Ardha-Magadhi at the Council of:
questions.rationale: The second Jain council at Vallabhi in Gujarat (512 CE), under Devardhigani, committed the Agamas to writing, preserving the Svetambara canon.
